summary:
Step 6 is ACCEPTABLE to commit. Both re-review findings are nitpicks and I reject both; nothing new was found, and I re-verified every claim the re-review was asked to judge.

(a) py-F1's fix as shipped is correct. `config_cb` is built exactly once, at Tools/semantic_store.ML:2299-2300, from the same `cfg_context` the driver is read from at :2295, and that `Remote_Procedure_Calling.callback'` VALUE is what travels: `check_embedding_service config_cb` (:2329 -> `callback = [config_cb]` at :2276), `interpret_cone driver config_cb force cone` (:2334 -> `interpret' driver config_cb (Context.Theory thy)` at :2032), the `Context.Proof` roots' direct `interpret' driver config_cb ctx` (:2339), then `send_for_interpretation` (:1884) -> `interpret_file_callbacks config_cb context` (:1858). `grep -n cfg_context Tools/semantic_store.ML` returns only :2286 (comment), :2292, :2295, :2300 — the parameter no longer exists below the entry point, and the duplicated `Config.make_config_lookup_callback` construction is gone (the two remaining ones, :2459 and :2475, are the pre-existing `embed_all_missing` / `query_knn` callers). No other caller of any of these functions exists anywhere in contrib/ (grepped .ML/.thy/.py).

Sharing one `callback'` across the cone's parallel RPCs is safe, and I checked this in RPC.ML rather than taking it on trust: `type callback' = {name, action: connection -> int -> unit}` (RPC.ML:436), and in `mk_callback` (:458-487) the only mutable cell, `val consumed = Unsynchronized.ref false` (:464), is allocated inside `fn conn => fn cb_id => Thread_Attributes.uninterruptible_body (fn run => let ...)`, i.e. per invocation, not per value. The captured function body (config.ML:41-51) only reads an immutable `Context.generic` and consults the registry under `registry_lock`. Concurrency is across connections anyway: `call_command` takes a distinct pooled connection per call (RPC.ML:913-923) and `call_command'` builds `local_tab` fresh per call (RPC.ML:566-567). The signature entry at :36-37 matches the definition at :1824-1825, the structure is transparently ascribed (`structure Semantic_Store : SEMANTIC_STORE`, :230), and the ML test's exactly-once assertion is load-bearing because `lookup_callback` checks `local_tab` first (RPC.ML:522-525) and `Strhashtab.update` lets a later duplicate name win silently.

(b) agreement-F3 behaves. I probed `Missing_Dimension` directly: `str()` is the bare sentence, `repr()` is `Missing_Dimension("...")`, `traceback.format_exception_only` renders the sentence, it survives pickling, and `isinstance(e, KeyError)` is still True — so the only `except KeyError` consumer of `dimension()`, `snapshot_sync._local_dimension` (snapshot_sync.py:290-296), is unchanged; the other two consumers (semantic_embedding.py:288, migrate_float32_to_q15.py:56) propagate. A live `dimension("no-such/model")` ends exactly with `Add it under 'dimension:'.`, which is what the new assertion pins.

(c) Plan §5.6 (SEMANTIC_CHANGE_GATE_PLAN.md:469-505) describes the shipped code, including the build-once/thread-the-callback wording, the `n_units = 0` guard, the placement after the opening block, and the corrected RPC-failure justification.

(d) Nothing regressed on the Python side. `Connection.semantic_vector_store = _conn_semantic_vector_store` (semantics.py:2841) with `warn` keyword-only, forwarded to `_resolve_embedding_config`, which gates only the warning and always raises (:2803-2805); `interpret_file` passes `warn=False` (semantic_interpretation.py:1747). The check's unit-in/unit-out RPC matches the `Semantic_Store.mark_interpreted` precedent (ML :362 `unpackUnit`, handler `async def _mark_interpreted(...) -> None` at semantics.py:2863). Provider construction really is side-effect free: `Embedding_Provider.__init__` (semantic_embedding.py:275-291) reads only the YAML plus `EMBEDDING_API_KEY`, and the diskcache is a lazy static opened at embed time (:313-321). `test_semantic_change_gate.py` alone: 37 passed; and re-run under a hostile `EMBEDDING_CONFIG_PATH` (a yaml with only text-embedding-3-large) plus junk `EMBEDDING_API_KEY`/`EMBEDDING_MODEL`: 37 passed again, so py-F2's hermeticity fix is real.

rulings.title: The startup check copies the opening block's `n_units = 0` guard instead of sharing it
rulings.rationale: The facts are right and the conclusion is wrong. Tools/semantic_store.ML:2321 and :2329 do both test `n_units = 0`, but `n_units` is an immutable `val` computed once at :2310, so the two guards cannot disagree at runtime — there is no failure, only a hypothesis about a future edit, which is exactly what the scope says to reject. There is also no plan/code disagreement: SEMANTIC_CHANGE_GATE_PLAN.md:484-486 writes "the opening block's own `n_units = 0` guard", which NAMES the condition (the same guard the block uses), and the code uses literally that expression on that value; it does not mandate one `if`. Two of the finding's supporting arguments are simply incorrect. First, fusing would not "encode derivation 3's ordering structurally instead of by adjacency": successive `val` bindings in an ML `let` are evaluated in order, so adjacency here IS sequencing — the fused `(vtr ...; check_embedding_service config_cb)` has exactly the same ordering guarantee, not a stronger one. Second, the fused form is not more elegant: it folds an outbound RPC into the binding whose job is to print a message, replaces two flat `val _ =` bindings (the Isabelle/ML idiom) with a parenthesized sequence expression inside one, and forces the two comments to merge although they justify different things — :2319-2320 says why the block is printed once before any parallel work, :2327-2328 says why a run with nothing to interpret has no prefilter to configure. Saving one line is not a review criterion.
rulings.fix: No change. Leave Tools/semantic_store.ML:2321-2329 as it stands.

rulings.title: `Missing_Dimension` is the only underscore-named exception class in the package
rulings.rationale: A style-only remark about letter case, with no failure, no plan disagreement, and no reader: the class name never reaches a user-visible Isabelle line (§12 #4's slot is `str(exc)`, which the subclass makes the bare sentence — I probed it), only a host-log traceback. The count inside Isabelle_Semantic_Embedding/ is accurate (I listed every top-level class: MissingPricing, SnapshotError, SnapshotBusy, ReachLimitError, RateLimitError, PoisonedSessionError, FatalAgentError, TransientAgentError are CamelCase), but the "convention" it infers does not survive one more grep. The file's own imported sibling class is underscore-styled — embedding_config.py:24 `from ._user_config import User_Config` — and across this author's other Python packages underscore-separated exception names are routine: ../Isa-Mini/IsaMini/AoA/model.py:651 `class AoA_Error(Exception)`, :3023 `class Interaction_BadAnswer(Exception)`, :1071 `class ArgumentError_UnknownProofOperation(ArgumentError)`, ../Theory-Agent-over-Trees/isabelle_theory_agent/exceptions.py:20 `class TAT_Error(Exception, ABC)` and four siblings, ../Isa-Mini/IsaMini/AoA/language_model_driver.py:45 `class Chat_Restart(Exception)`. So both spellings are the user's own habit, and which one "should" win here is a preference, not a defect — the finding's own fix text concedes as much by making the remedy conditional on the user picking a side. The finding further overstates its warrant: it claims "the SCOPE asks explicitly whether the name fits the package's conventions", and it does not — SCOPE.md:234-236 asks only whether every `except KeyError` consumer still works, about `str()`/`repr()`, and whether anything depended on the repr. All three I verified hold.
rulings.fix: No change. Leave `Missing_Dimension` at Isabelle_Semantic_Embedding/embedding_config.py:46 as it is; do not churn a two-reference name over casing.
